summary.one_line: A Thane/Kolkata-based HVAC and electromechanical EPC and O&M contractor whose revenue rose about 20x in two years after a February 2025 change of control. Growth has come with deeply negative operating cash flow, heavy customer concentration, no demonstrable moat and several governance flags tied to the new promoters' group. An all-fresh SME issue is the only clear positive.
bull_points: Rapid scale-up: revenue from operations rose from Rs 13.49 cr (FY24) to Rs 108.61 cr (FY25) and Rs 277.63 cr (FY26), with Rs 97.31 cr in Q1 FY27 alone. EBITDA margin has held at about 14.4% for FY25, FY26 and Q1 FY27 (S1).

Order book was Rs 491.12 cr across 21 projects at 30 June 2026, about 1.8x FY26 revenue. It includes Rs 120 cr of new data-centre work orders from the Indian arm of a global cloud company and a listed real-estate developer (S1, S9).
The issue is 100% fresh, 1,03,62,000 shares with no offer for sale, so all the money goes to the company. The promoters are not selling (S1, S2).
Reported leverage is modest: total borrowings were Rs 30.88 cr against net worth of Rs 109.69 cr (debt/equity 0.28) at 30 June 2026 (S1, S2).

The markets it serves are growing. D&B, in a report commissioned for the issue, sizes India's HVAC EPC I&C market at Rs 81,284 cr in FY25, rising to Rs 1,69,723 cr by FY30 (15.9% CAGR). It projects data-centre HVAC EPC growth of 22% a year (S1).
bear_points: Profit is not turning into cash. Operating cash flow was -Rs 8.94 cr in FY25, -Rs 46.85 cr in FY26 and -Rs 11.16 cr in Q1 FY27, against cumulative PAT of about Rs 51.5 cr since FY24. Receivables reached Rs 100.56 cr and inventory Rs 52.82 cr by June 2026 (S1).

Most of the proceeds plug the working-capital hole. Rs 70 cr of the Rs 116.05 cr issue goes to long-term working capital and Rs 25.53 cr to heavy equipment. The company's own projections have the net working-capital gap rising to Rs 331.61 cr by FY28 (S1, S2).
Customer concentration is high: the top 5 customers were 78.65% of FY26 revenue and 82.85% in Q1 FY27, and the largest single customer was 26.99% of FY26 revenue (S1).

Governance flags. In March 2026 the ED provisionally attached Rs 11.88 cr of the promoter's shares in promoter-group company Ganesh Infraworld in a PMLA matter. All three independent directors also sit on Ganesh Infraworld's board. The RHP says promoter-group company Tykoon Mines was paid Rs 29.60 cr in equipment rent in FY26, but its own related-party note shows no FY26 transaction with Tykoon (S1).
Compliance record: 13 delayed RoC filings (one 1,645 days late), several statutory records that cannot be traced, repeated late PF/ESI/GST payments, and a GST show-cause notice for Rs 2.15 cr (S1).
watch_points: Whether operating cash flow turns positive in FY27 once the IPO money is deployed, or receivables and inventory keep outgrowing revenue (S1).
The outcome of the ED/PMLA matter involving Ganesh Infraworld. The freeze was lifted on 20 May 2026 and Ganesh told NSE in August 2026 that no attachment continues against the company (S1, S12).
Whether the promoter-group equipment rental with Tykoon Mines shrinks after the Rs 25.53 cr capex, and how it is disclosed in the first listed annual report (S1).
Conversion of the Rs 120 cr data-centre EPIC orders. Data-centre revenue so far is from one O&M client (S1).
Final category-wise subscription. No figures were published on the trackers checked at the time of writing (S3, S5, S11).

reasoning: The track record is very short and was largely built after the change of control. The current promoters bought 100% of the company in February 2025, at an adjusted Rs 3.42 per share. Revenue then went from Rs 13.49 cr (FY24) to Rs 277.63 cr (FY26), led by onshore EPIC orders and backed by earthmoving equipment rented from a promoter-group company. This is an 18-month build by owners whose background is civil EPC, not a seasoned HVAC franchise; the RHP itself concedes the promoters have limited HVAC experience (S1).

The growth consumes cash, and the IPO mainly refills it. Cumulative operating cash flow since FY24 is about -Rs 66.8 cr against about Rs 51.5 cr of cumulative PAT. Rs 70 cr of the proceeds goes to working capital, and management's own projection still has the working-capital gap rising to Rs 331.61 cr by FY28. Money raised here pays for receivables rather than building a durable asset (S1, S2).

There is no real moat. The RHP names no competitor and offers only the claim that there is no 'apple-to-apple' peer. Work is mostly won by tender at 17-33% bid success rates. The top 5 customers make up roughly 79-83% of revenue, and FY26 revenue of Rs 277.6 cr is a fraction of a percent of a Rs 94,026 cr (FY26P) HVAC EPC market (S1).

Governance quality is below what a retail investor should accept, for four reasons. The promoter's shares in a group company were provisionally attached by the ED (since unfrozen, matter not closed). All three independent directors sit on that same group company's board. The RHP's own figures for Rs 29.60 cr of FY26 equipment rent paid to promoter-group Tykoon Mines do not appear in the related-party note. And there is a long history of late statutory filings and payments (S1, S12).

The structure is the one positive. The issue is all fresh capital with no OFS, promoters stay at about 53.5% post-issue, and promoters' contribution is locked in for 3 years. These are real positives, but they do not offset the cash-flow and governance concerns, and other pre-IPO holders who came in at about Rs 79 per share (adjusted) face only a 1-year lock-in (S1, S2).

subsections.title: What Ravita actually does and how it earns revenue

blocks.text: Ravita is a project contractor. It does engineering, procurement, installation and commissioning (EPIC) of HVAC systems, central air-conditioning, chiller plants, industrial compressors and cooling equipment. It also does operation and maintenance (O&M) of such systems, including systems installed by others (S1). Every rupee of revenue is booked as 'EPC and O&M contracts' won directly from clients. The RHP reports no sub-contract revenue in any period (S1). The company was incorporated in December 2007 as Sayo Construction Pvt Ltd, became Powermech Services Pvt Ltd in 2010, and took the Ravita name only in September 2025 (S1).

Pricing is either item-rate (bill-of-quantities unit rates paid on actual quantities) or percentage-rate (a premium or discount to the client's estimate) for projects. O&M is priced cost-plus with inflation adjustment and billed monthly. EPIC projects run 6-14 months with 6-9 month defect-liability periods, and O&M contracts run 12-36 months (S1). In practice O&M has been short-tenor: at June 2026 there were 3 O&M contracts of up to 1 year, 5 of 1-3 years and none longer (S1).

blocks.caption: Revenue by segment (Rs lakh; % of total income) - RHP p.182
EPIC vs O&M revenue (Rs lakh) - RHP p.183

blocks.text: The business has changed character. In FY24 it was an O&M shop (85% of revenue) with Rs 13.5 cr of turnover. After the February 2025 change of control it became a project-EPIC business (85% of Q1 FY27 revenue). Project revenue is lumpier, more working-capital hungry and less recurring than the O&M base it grew from (S1).

Onshore covers commercial, hospitality, corporate-park and industrial HVAC in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Odisha and Karnataka. The largest live onshore jobs are an HVAC contract for an Ahmedabad metal recycler (Rs 80.37 cr contract value), a factory HVAC job (Rs 60.07 cr) and a Rs 91.65 cr hybrid order for a renewable-energy company in Karnataka (S1). Offshore covers HVAC work on rigs and platforms in Indian territorial waters: 6 rigs and 16 associated platforms in the last three years plus Q1 FY27 (S1, S9). The RHP's history says the first offshore EPIC/O&M job was for a PSU oil E&P company in 2016, but it does not name the client (S1). Also classified as offshore is a sub-sea effluent discharge pipeline for Numaligarh Refinery's crude terminal at Paradip, Odisha (Rs 77.20 cr contract) (S1, S9).

Data Centre has so far been O&M for a single client, Reliance Corporate IT Park at Navi Mumbai, served since 2013-14. Data-centre revenue came from 1 client in every period disclosed (S1). Rs 120 cr of new data-centre EPIC orders are new: Rs 55 cr from the Indian subsidiary of a global technology and cloud company and Rs 65 cr from a listed real-estate developer, both in Maharashtra (S1, S9).

blocks.caption: Customer and supplier concentration - RHP pp.24-25, 296

blocks.text: Geography is equally concentrated. The western region (Maharashtra, Gujarat, territorial waters) made up 86.96% of FY26 revenue. Odisha, largely the Numaligarh job, was 40.88% of Q1 FY27 revenue (S1). FY26 territorial-waters revenue (Rs 74.93 cr) exactly equals FY26 largest-customer revenue, which means the offshore segment is effectively one client (S1). By customer type, government/PSU work was 35.47% of FY26 revenue and private clients 64.53% (S1).

Ravita is asset-light on paper. Net PP&E was only Rs 9.30 cr at June 2026, mostly scaffolding (over 7,000 sets), ladders, access platforms, tools and seven modular containers (S1). Heavy machinery is rented. The objects chapter discloses that since August 2025 the company has rented 41 earthmoving machines (30 dumpers, 8 excavators, 2 dozers, 1 grader) from its group company Tykoon Mines GK Ltd, at about Rs 3.70 cr a month. Rent was Rs 29.60 cr in FY26 and Rs 11.10 cr in Q1 FY27 (S1).

An HVAC contractor renting 30 dumpers and 8 excavators is unusual. The 'major projects' listed in the RHP's industry chapter are also largely civil and pipeline jobs: Sasan UMPP intake pipeline repair, metro barricading boards, a temporary access bridge for the Versova-Bandra Sea Link, and ethane pipeline structure fabrication (S1). Investors should read the 'HVAC specialist' label with some scepticism. A meaningful part of the post-2025 growth appears to be civil/earthwork-heavy execution.

Work is won through competitive tenders on e-procurement portals and through non-tender nomination. Tender revenue fell from 87.6% of FY24 revenue to 46.3% in Q1 FY27 (S1). Bid success rates for onshore were 26.58% in FY26 and 22.22% in Q1 FY27 (S1). Execution relies on a vendor network of more than 100 vendors and on contract labour: 246 contract workers alongside 399 employees at June 2026 (S1).

items: Employees: 399 (Q1 FY27), 398 (FY26), 615 (FY25), 321 (FY24). Attrition was 62.82% in FY26 and 82.03% in FY24, which the company attributes to moving staff onto contract labour (S1).

Offices: the registered office (CBD Belapur, Navi Mumbai) and a warehouse (Nhava, Raigad) are rented, both on leases ending in early 2027. The corporate office in Salt Lake, Kolkata is rented from promoter Starwings Realtors until March 2032 (S1).
The only owned property is a vacant commercial unit at Raheja Tesla Industrial Park, Thane, which is mortgaged to ICICI Bank (S1).
Trademarks were applied for only in March 2026 and are not yet registered (S1).

blocks.text: The only industry source in the RHP is a Dun & Bradstreet report dated March 2026, commissioned and paid for by the company for this issue (S1). It sizes India's industrial HVAC market at Rs 1,45,000 cr in FY25 and projects Rs 2,87,862 cr by FY30 (S1). The two pools Ravita actually sells into are HVAC EPC I&C (installation and commissioning) and HVAC O&M (S1, S9).

blocks.caption: HVAC EPC I&C and O&M market by location (Rs cr) - D&B report in RHP pp.150-155

blocks.text: The data-centre tailwind is the most compelling part of the story. D&B cites India data-centre capacity rising from 950 MW (FY24) to 2,070 MW (FY25), with a projection of 3,400 MW by FY30, and Rs 500-550 bn of investment expected over FY25-27 (S1). Offshore growth is slower: D&B projects 11.7% CAGR, and western-offshore crude output, where Ravita's rigs are, fell from 14.24 MMT in FY21 to 12.47 MMT in FY25 (S1).

Scale check (our arithmetic on RHP figures): Ravita's FY26 revenue of Rs 277.6 cr is about 0.3% of D&B's Rs 94,026 cr FY26P EPC I&C market alone. The market is large enough that Ravita's growth is not constrained by demand. That also means its growth tells you nothing about competitive strength (S1).

The RHP names no competitor, listed or unlisted. Its industry chapter claims 'there is no direct apple-to-apple peer that matches Ravita's integrated execution and service model' and describes the market as fragmented and relationship-driven (S1). The RHP gives no market-share figure, no import-substitution claim, no proprietary technology, no OEM licence and no regulatory barrier (S1). Its trademarks are not even registered yet (S1).

items: Offshore experience is a genuine but narrow qualification. Working on rigs requires safety-certified crews and client pre-qualification. However, the offshore order book has shrunk to Rs 70.13 cr (14.3% of the book), offshore bid success was 0% on 3 bids in Q1 FY27, and the segment is effectively one client (S1).

The data-centre relationship with Reliance Corporate IT Park dates from 2013-14 and is sticky O&M work. But it is a single client, and data-centre revenue barely grew from Rs 30.81 cr (FY25) to Rs 33.15 cr (FY26) (S1).
Onshore EPIC, the growth engine, is won largely by tender at 17-27% success rates in a market the RHP itself calls fragmented. That is the opposite of a moat (S1).
Repeat-client revenue fell from 100% (FY24) to 62.27% (Q1 FY27). Over half of FY26 revenue came from clients of under 3 years' standing (S1).

blocks.text: Verdict on moat: none demonstrated. Ravita is a contractor competing on price and relationships in a fragmented, tender-driven market. Its two niches (offshore rig HVAC, one data-centre O&M client) are real experience but each depends on a single customer. The 'no apple-to-apple peer' line is the standard prospectus claim, not a barrier to entry (S1).

blocks.caption: Restated profit and loss (Rs cr) - RHP pp.69, 257, 273, 285

blocks.text: Revenue grew 705% in FY25 and 156% in FY26 (S1, S8). The MD&A attributes this to onshore project awards rising from 5 (Rs 52.53 cr contract value) in FY25 to 20 (Rs 324.28 cr) in FY26, and to the Numaligarh offshore pipeline job (S1). The blended gross margin compressed from 38.39% (FY24) to 20.19% (FY26) as the mix moved to lower-margin onshore EPIC (16.55% GM), against data centre at 30.37% and offshore at 23.44% (S1). EBITDA margin stabilised at 14.4% only because overheads stayed tiny: employee cost was just Rs 3.01 cr in FY26, because most site labour sits in cost of services (S1).

The near-identical EBITDA margin of 14.4% in FY25, FY26 and Q1 FY27 is unusual for a lumpy project contractor whose segment mix swung sharply between these periods. Equipment rent of Rs 29.60 cr (FY26) and Rs 11.10 cr (Q1 FY27) paid to promoter-group Tykoon Mines sits inside cost of services (S1). Margins therefore depend partly on a related-party price. FY25 PAT also includes a one-off key-man insurance receipt of Rs 0.62 cr (S1).

subsections.title: Balance sheet and the cash-flow problem

blocks.caption: Balance sheet and cash flow (Rs cr) - RHP pp.68, 70, 256, 258

blocks.text: This is the central financial red flag. From FY24 to Q1 FY27 the company reported cumulative PAT of about Rs 51.5 cr while burning about Rs 66.8 cr of operating cash (our sum of RHP figures) (S1). Receivable days have stayed around 88-100 against stated terms of 30-90 days. Inventory, odd for a services contractor, grew to Rs 52.82 cr. Advances to suppliers and EMD/security deposits added a further Rs 34.12 cr of short-term loans and advances by June 2026 (S1). Chanakya's pre-issue review flagged the same need to check receivables and operating cash flow (S7).

The gap has been funded by three things (S1). First, a Rs 56.39 cr pre-IPO equity raise in June-August 2025: 35,241 shares at Rs 16,000 each, about Rs 79 per current share after the split and bonus. That raise alone explains most of the jump in net worth from Rs 15.13 cr to Rs 99.56 cr. Second, supplier credit. Third, related-party and inter-corporate loans, including a Rs 12.04 cr inter-corporate deposit at 10% from promoter Starwings Realtors in Q1 FY27 (S1). So the improvement in debt/equity from 1.53 to 0.28 came from new equity, not from cash generated by the business (S1).

items: Rs 19.02 cr of unsecured loans are repayable on demand. Inter-corporate deposits outstanding (Rs 13.06 cr) are about six times their stated sanction of Rs 2.20 cr (S1).

ICICI Bank is the only bank lender: a Rs 12 cr cash credit line and a Rs 9 cr bank-guarantee line. The line is secured partly by fixed deposits placed by promoter-group company Ganesh Infraworld and by the promoters' personal guarantees (S1).
Contingent liabilities are Rs 4.47 cr of indirect-tax claims not acknowledged as debt. The RHP describes only one GST notice, for Rs 2.15 cr (S1).
No contract-asset or unbilled-revenue line is disclosed, and no provision is held against receivables (S1).

subsections.title: Does the trend support the growth story?

blocks.text: Partly. The order book is real on its face: Rs 491.12 cr at June 2026 versus Rs 83.87 cr at March 2025, with Rs 558.90 cr of fresh orders won in FY26 (S1). Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 97.31 cr suggests FY27 can exceed FY26 (S1, S8). But each step-up in revenue has required a bigger step-up in working capital. The company's own projection in the objects chapter has receivables rising to Rs 226.11 cr and the net working-capital gap to Rs 331.61 cr by FY28 (S1).
The growth is real on the P&L but has not yet produced a rupee of free cash. Until operating cash flow turns positive, reported profit is a claim on future collections, not a demonstrated return.

Return metrics also need context. The RHP's 48.90% FY26 RoNW and 128.31% FY25 RoNW are calculated on a tiny pre-placement equity base (S1, S2). Q1 FY27 RoNW of 9.68% (not annualised) on the enlarged base is the more representative figure (S1).

blocks.text: Date and price discrepancy. The RHP dated 6 Oct 2026 shows anchor bidding on 12 Oct and the issue open 13-15 Oct, with the price band left blank (S1). PTI-syndicated releases of 13 Oct and several aggregators carry the same 13-15 dates (S9, S16). Later sources (Chittorgarh, InvestorGain, IPO Watch and an ANI release) show anchors on 13 Oct and bidding 14-16 Oct (S2, S4, S10, S11, S18). We could not open the addendum or advertisement that moved the dates, so investors should confirm the closing date with their broker. The Rs 105-112 band is reported consistently by multiple sources, and anchors were allotted at Rs 112 (S3, S5, S9).

Because the whole issue is fresh, all of the gross proceeds of about Rs 116.05 cr at the upper band go to the company, less issue expenses (S1, S2). The promoter and promoter group will not take part in the issue (S1). The DRHP was filed with NSE Emerge in March 2026 (S15). The company then trimmed the issue from up to 1.25 crore shares in that draft to 1.04 crore shares in the RHP (S8).

blocks.text: About 60% of the issue goes to working capital (S1, S2). The objects are unappraised by any bank, and unused amounts may roll into FY28-FY29 (S1). The working-capital estimate assumes receivable days of 93-94 and payable days falling to 40 by FY28. The projected working-capital gap of Rs 211.33 cr (FY27) and Rs 331.61 cr (FY28) is funded largely by 'internal accruals' that, on the historic cash-flow record, have not yet materialised (S1). The DRHP had earmarked Rs 66 cr for working capital and Rs 25.09 cr for equipment, per Chanakya's review of the draft (S7).

blocks.caption: Equipment to be bought from issue proceeds - RHP pp.118-119

blocks.text: The stated rationale for the capex is to cut reliance on equipment rented, at about Rs 3.70 cr a month, from group company Tykoon Mines (S1). Owning trucks and dumpers is cheaper than paying a related party Rs 44 cr a year, so in principle this is a good use of money. It also confirms that a large part of what IPO money is funding is earthmoving and haulage capacity rather than HVAC capability. And it leaves open why such large rentals were struck with a promoter entity in the first place.

The promoters are Vibhoar Agrawal (40, B.Com, about 7 years' experience, Chairman and Executive Director), his wife Rachita Agrawal (36, B.Com and fashion-design diploma), and their 50:50-owned Kolkata real-estate company Starwings Realtors Pvt Ltd, incorporated in 2022 (S1). They acquired 100% of the company in February 2025 from the founding Goswami family, at Rs 691 per Rs 10 share, which works out to Rs 3.42 per current share (S1). Vibhoar Agrawal is also Managing Director of NSE Emerge-listed civil EPC company Ganesh Infraworld Ltd, which Vivro also took public in December 2024 (S1, S13). He sits on the boards of Tykoon Mines GK and several other group entities (S1). The RHP itself lists limited promoter experience in HVAC as a risk (S1).

The operating continuity comes from Sunildutt Narayan Goswami (60), the previous promoter, now MD and CEO. He is a former merchant-marine chief engineer and Chartered Engineer who has been a director since 2010, with remuneration of up to Rs 89.70 lakh a year (S1). A COO, Bhaskar Agnihotri (marine engineering), was hired in July 2026 at Rs 108 lakh a year, more than the MD's pay. The CFO (since June 2025) and the Company Secretary (since March 2026) are recent appointments (S1).

blocks.caption: Pre- and post-issue shareholding - RHP pp.97-104; Chittorgarh

items: Lock-in: 20% of post-issue capital is locked in as promoters' contribution for 3 years. Of the promoters' excess holding, 50% is locked for 2 years and 50% for 1 year (S1).
All other pre-IPO shareholders, including the 2025 placement investors who paid about Rs 79 per share adjusted, are locked in for only 1 year (S1).
Anchor shares: 50% locked for 30 days and 50% for 90 days (S1, S3).

blocks.text: Unlike most SME RPT sections, this one is not routine. The related-party web runs through the promoters' own group, on both the cost side and the financing side (S1).

blocks.caption: Key related-party dealings (Rs lakh) - RHP pp.72-74, 117, 275-276, 297-299
rows: Tykoon Mines GK (group co; Vibhoar Agrawal a director)
2,960.00 per objects chapter; nil in Note 35
FDs pledged as security for Ravita's ICICI limits; JV partner (60%) in Ganesh Netsoft JV

blocks.text: Disclosure inconsistency. The objects chapter (p.117) states Ravita paid Tykoon Mines Rs 2,960 lakh of equipment rent in FY26, roughly 10.7% of FY26 revenue on our arithmetic. The restated related-party note (Note 35, p.275) records rent to Tykoon only in Q1 FY27 and shows nil for FY26 (S1). Either a Rs 29.6 cr related-party payment is missing from the audited RPT note, or the relationship was not treated as related in FY26 even though Vibhoar Agrawal was already a Ravita director from March 2025. Either way it is a disclosure-quality failure on the single largest related-party flow.

Tykoon Mines GK was formerly Kandoi Transport Ltd (S1). A company registry aggregator lists Kandoi Transport as a Cuttack, Odisha company in transport-support activities whose last filed balance sheet was for March 2023 (S14). Tykoon's registered office is listed at Ravita's own Belapur office address (S1). The corporate office, Starwings' office and Ganesh Infraworld share the same Salt Lake, Kolkata address (S1).

All three independent directors were appointed on 8 October 2025, and all three also sit on the board of promoter-group company Ganesh Infraworld (S1). Golock Chandra Sahoo is also on Tykoon Mines' board, the related-party equipment lessor (S1). Rupal Haria, who chairs the audit committee, also sits on the boards of other Vivro-managed SME issuers (S1). The RHP considers them independent, but an audit committee drawn entirely from the promoter's other listed company is weak oversight for a business with this much related-party flow.

ED/PMLA matter: on 20 January 2026 the Enforcement Directorate searched Ganesh Infraworld (formerly Ganesh International) over alleged availment of Rs 1,188 lakh of input tax credit through a shell entity. On 30 March 2026, Vibhoar Agrawal's shareholding in Ganesh worth Rs 1,188 lakh was provisionally attached (S1). The NSDL freeze was lifted on 20 May 2026 (S1). In an August 2026 NSE filing, Ganesh said the search was initiated against the partnership firm Ganesh International, that no proceedings had been initiated against the company, and that no attachment continues against its assets (S12). The RHP lists the matter under criminal proceedings but says elsewhere that there are no regulatory actions against promoters (S1).

items: 13 delayed RoC filings, including an auditor appointment form 1,645 days late and a DPT-3 940 days late. Multiple historical filings and challans (FY08-FY23) cannot be traced, and copies were requested from the RoC only in March 2026 (S1).
Repeated late statutory dues: PF delayed in 9, 8 and 4 instances in FY24, FY25 and FY26. GST of Rs 322.23 lakh was paid late in FY25 (S1).

A GST show-cause notice covering FY20-FY24 alleges ineligible ITC, misclassification and reverse-charge non-payment, with a Rs 214.62 lakh demand. There is also a Rs 110.68 lakh commercial suit by a sub-contractor (S1).
Promoter-group entity M.R. Foods Pvt Ltd faces compulsory strike-off, which could trigger disqualification of Vibhoar Agrawal as a director under s.164(2) (S1).

Lead-manager record: Vivro's 11 SME IPOs show 30-day returns ranging from +278.5% to -25.0%. It also managed Ganesh Infraworld's IPO, which raised Rs 98.58 cr mainly for working capital and listed at a 90% premium (S1, S13).

Working capital and cash flow. Operating cash flow has been negative in FY25, FY26 and Q1 FY27 (-Rs 46.85 cr in FY26). Receivables of Rs 100.56 cr are about equal to the company's entire net worth. A delay by one large client could force fresh borrowing or dilution (S1).

Customer concentration. The top 5 customers account for 78.65% of FY26 and 82.85% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Offshore and data centre are each effectively single-client businesses, and the order book's top 5 clients account for 67.05% of it (S1).

Tender dependence and execution. Most new work is won by tender at 17-33% success rates. The two largest projects make up 31.90% of the Rs 491.12 cr order book. Average order size jumped from Rs 0.96 cr (FY24) to Rs 27.91 cr (Q1 FY27), well beyond anything the company executed before 2025 (S1).
Related-party cost base. About 11% of revenue went in equipment rent to a promoter-group company in Q1 FY27. Margins and the capex rationale therefore depend on terms set within the group (S1).

blocks.text: These risks reinforce one another. The business has grown by taking on larger, more concentrated, tender-won projects that tie up cash. It funds the gap with promoter-group loans and IPO money while relying on promoter-group equipment. A single dispute or delayed payment on a top project would hit revenue, cash and covenants at the same time (S1).

Workforce instability: attrition was 62.82% in FY26 and 82.03% in FY24, and off-roll labour rose to 22.75% of manpower cost. For a site-execution business with offshore safety exposure, that is an operational risk the RHP does not quantify (S1).

items: Promoter-group legal exposure. The ED/PMLA matter around Ganesh Infraworld is not formally closed before the Adjudicating Authority. The M.R. Foods strike-off could disqualify the chairman as a director (S1, S12).
Short ownership history. The current promoters have controlled the company only since February 2025 and have limited HVAC experience (S1).

Disclosure quality. The FY26 Tykoon rent is missing from the RPT note. Ratios differ between Notes 31 and 34. Historical statutory records are untraceable. The MD&A still refers to the 'Draft Red Herring Prospectus' (S1).
Pending tax demands. Indirect-tax claims total Rs 446.66 lakh, of which only Rs 214.62 lakh is explained (S1).

SME liquidity and lock-in. After the 1-year lock-in, the roughly 26% of pre-issue capital held by non-promoter investors becomes free to sell. Much of it was bought in the 2025 placements at about Rs 79 a share adjusted. Trading on NSE Emerge is in lots of 1,200 shares, which limits exits (S1, S2).

blocks.text: Most of the RHP's remaining 79 risk factors are generic (interest rates, insurance cover, dividend policy, macro). The items above are the ones that would change an investment decision (S1).

Management has given no revenue or margin guidance. The concrete forward statements are three. First, in the IPO press release, Chairman Vibhoar Agrawal said deploying proceeds into working capital and heavy equipment will 'strengthen our in-house project delivery capabilities as we expand our presence, including in the data centre segment' (S9). Second, the RHP's strategy section lists expansion into luxury hospitality, shipyards (an approved-supplier application has been made with a large shipyard), pharma, airports and data centres; geographic expansion; more selective, margin-focused bidding; and building smart-building/BMS capability (S1). Third, the MD&A says no new business segments are expected (S1).

blocks.caption: Management's own working-capital projection (Rs lakh) - RHP pp.112-113

blocks.text: The working-capital projection, certified by the statutory auditor and approved by the board on 6 October 2026, implies management expects the business to roughly triple its working-capital base again by FY28. That is an implicit high-growth plan, though no revenue figure is attached (S1). The visible pipeline is the Rs 491.12 cr order book and a bid book of Rs 1,407.40 cr (S1).

Our read: management's plan is more of the same. Bigger tendered projects, financed by more working capital, with data centres as the new growth narrative. Nothing in the disclosures suggests a plan to fix cash conversion. The projection holds receivable days at about 94 and assumes payables shrink.

subsections.title: Anchors, subscription so far and grey market

blocks.text: Anchor book: 15 anchor investors were allotted 29,48,400 shares at Rs 112, about Rs 33.02 cr or 28.45% of the issue (S3, S5). The largest allocations were Rs 5.00 cr each to 360 ONE Prime, Finavenue Capital Trust (Finavenue Growth Fund) and Navbharat Investment Trust, and Rs 2.49 cr to Kingsman Wealth Fund PCC-KIF II (S3, S5). Half the anchor shares (14,74,200) are locked in for 30 days and half for 90 days (S3, S5).

Subscription: at the time of writing (14 Oct 2026), no category-wise subscription figures had been published on the trackers we checked. Chittorgarh and InvestorGain showed no data, and IPO Watch and IPO Ji showed placeholders or zeros (S3, S5, S11, S17). This report is written on the opening day of bidding on the 14-16 Oct schedule, so any day-1 figures would be partial anyway. Readers should not infer demand either way from their absence.

Grey market premium (unofficial, unregulated and not an investment signal): InvestorGain reported a GMP of Rs 2 on 14 Oct 2026, down from a peak of Rs 12 on 10 Oct (S6). Chanakya's review cited about Rs 4 a few days earlier (S7). The quick fade is itself a sign of lukewarm informal demand, but this report's call does not rest on it.

items: Third-party reviews were mixed. Chanakya rated the issue 'Selective Apply, subject to verification', 3/5, with overall risk 'High' (S7). InvestorGain shows a 3/5 team rating (S4).
Allotment is expected around 19 Oct and listing around 22 Oct 2026 on NSE Emerge on the revised schedule (S2, S4).

method: Primary source: the full Red Herring Prospectus dated 6 Oct 2026 (S1), downloaded from the lead manager Vivro's site. The PDF's text layer was compressed, so pages were read as rendered page images. The relevant chapters were read in full: risk factors, capital structure, objects, industry overview (D&B report), business, management, promoters and group companies, restated financials including the related-party note, MD&A, financial indebtedness, and litigation. Key items (Tykoon equipment rent on p.117, related-party Note 35 on p.275, the ED matter on p.302) were rechecked directly on the page images. Figures were converted from Rs lakh to Rs cr; derived numbers (cumulative PAT vs operating cash flow, Tykoon rent as % of revenue, market-share estimate) are our own arithmetic and labelled as such. The March 2026 DRHP on NSE timed out and was not read; DRHP-stage object amounts are taken from Chanakya's review (S7). Secondary sources were used for the price band, revised dates, anchor allocation, GMP and subscription status (S2-S11). Material gaps and conflicts: (1) the RHP prints bid dates of 13-15 Oct, while later trackers and an ANI release show 14-16 Oct with anchors on 13 Oct; we could not open the addendum confirming the change. (2) The price band is blank in the RHP; Rs 105-112 comes from multiple secondary sources and the Rs 112 anchor price. (3) No subscription figures had been published at the time of writing. (4) The Ganesh Infraworld NSE letter (S12) and several aggregator pages timed out or were blocked, so they are cited from search-result content only and marked as such; publication dates for aggregator pages are access dates. (5) The RHP names neither the offshore anchor client nor any competitor. Valuation (P/E, market-cap multiples, peer comparison) is deliberately excluded per the brief, even where sources volunteered it.
